# Unframed whole-space normality on the attained normal span

This note removes the extra fixed frame from the generic-budget
whole-space-cover stress. It preserves the original cap count. Its
contacts are still contacts in continuous space, and are not asserted
to lie in the actual source fibers. The resulting source tensor
identity is exact, but no OC cap-budget inequality is inferred.

## 1. Setting and attained value

Use the source and cap definitions in
candidate b488285aaeabe80d (candidate b488285aaeabe80d):
`n>=0,d>=1`, finite nonempty `P subset Z^n`, positive full-dimensional
polytope fibers `K_z`, source measure `mu`, and total mass `M`.
There are exactly `N` caps, all with variable continuous unit normals,

`L_i(z,x)=a_i dot z+u_i dot x-b_i`, `|u_i|=1`.

The caps must cover all of `R^d` above every `z in P`. Let `v(tau)`
be the minimum of `Psi=sum_i int(L_i)_+ dmu` under this requirement
and the budgets `c_i=mu{L_i>=0}<=tau M`.

The unframed attainment theorem in Section 2 of the cited note applies.
The same finite polytope formulas and balanced-certificate quantifiers
show that `v` is semialgebraic. Consequently it is `C^1` and locally
Lipschitz outside finitely many interior feasible budgets. Fix one
such regular budget and an attained minimizer.

## 2. Remove the dispensable normal-face caps

Let `A=conv{u_1,...,u_N}`. Whole-space coverage implies `0 in A`.
Let `F` be the smallest face of this polytope containing zero, and
put `V=span F`. Then `0` belongs to the relative interior of `F`,
and `F` contains a relative ball about zero in `V`.

Every nonnegative balanced relation

`lambda in Delta_N`, `sum_i lambda_i u_i=0`

is supported on the normals lying in `F`. To prove this, expose the
face `F` by a linear functional which vanishes on `F` and is strictly
positive at every `u_i` outside it. Applying that functional to the
balanced relation forces every outside coefficient to be zero. The
case `F=A` needs no exposing functional and has the same conclusion.

For each base index, whole-space coverage has a balanced certificate
`sum_i lambda_i(b_i-a_i dot z)<=0`. The preceding observation shows
that the caps with normals in `F` already cover whole `R^d` above
every base. Thus caps outside `F` are dispensable. At a hinge
minimizer they must all have zero hinge: replacing any such cap by
an empty source cap would otherwise decrease the objective while
preserving coverage and budgets. Zero hinge also implies zero source
cap mass, because a nonvertical cap of positive volume contains a
positive-volume set with strictly positive margin.

Replace every outside cap by an empty source cap with a unit normal
chosen in `V`, zero integer tilt, and a sufficiently large finite
offset. This does not change the attained value or any budget and
does not change the cap count. All resulting normals lie in `V`, and

`0 in int_V conv{u_i}`.                                     (1)

Here `r=dim V>=1`: the zero-dimensional face `{0}` cannot be a face
of a polytope whose listed vertices all have norm one, since a
zero-dimensional face is a vertex and must be one of those vertices.

This replacement selects a minimizing representative. The theorem
below is asserted for this representative; it does not claim that
every dispensable original normal admits the same individual stress.

## 3. A smooth local rank parameterization

Let `v_i` range over the unit sphere of the fixed subspace `V`, near
the representative normals, and let `R` range over rotations near
the identity. Parameterize the physical normals by

`u_i=R v_i`.

All integer tilts and offsets remain free. Redundancy of this smooth
parameterization causes no difficulty: the exact-penalty argument
takes place in its product coordinate space.

Condition (1) persists for nearby `v_i`. There is a fixed `epsilon>0`
such that the convex hull of the nearby `v_i` contains
`epsilon B_V`. Hence

`max_i[v_i dot x+a_i dot z-b_i]>=epsilon |x|-T_z`

for `x in V` and a locally bounded threshold constant `T_z`.
The whole-space coverage value is

`F_z=inf_(x in V) max_i[v_i dot x+a_i dot z-b_i]`.             (2)

It is finite and locally Lipschitz, and its contacts are locally
bounded in `V`. The proof restricts the coercive minimization to one
fixed sufficiently large cube in `V`, as in the fixed-frame argument.
Its optimal contacts lie strictly inside that cube. The physical
rotation `R` does not occur in (2), because rotating all normals
merely changes the continuous coordinate used in the infimum.
Thus whole-space coverage is exactly invariant under a common
rotation of all continuous normals.

The uniform offset repair `b_i -> b_i-G`, where
`G=max(0,max_z(-F_z))`, restores coverage and changes the parameter
vector by exactly `sqrt(N)G`. It stays in this rank parameterization.

Although the local variations use a fixed rank, their resulting covers
are feasible covers in the original unrestricted problem. Therefore
the GLOBAL attained value `v(max_i c_i/M)` is still a lower bound for
their hinge. The generic-budget exact penalty proof applies without
having to define or assume regularity of a separate rank-restricted
value function.

## 4. Normal stress and consistent moments

At the selected minimizer there are nonnegative multipliers `r_i`
for the budgets and `eta_z` for coverage, with objective multiplier
one, active-constraint complementarity, and

`M sum_i r_i=-v'(tau)`.                                     (3)

For cap `i`, let `tau_i` be its consistent effective coarea section
measure, with density in `[0,1]` on `K_z intersect {L_i=0}` and the
usual unit-normal coarea convention. Put

`S_i=int d tau_i`, `Z_i^s=int z d tau_i`, `X_i^s=int x d tau_i`,
`Z_i=int_Hi z dmu`, `X_i=int_Hi x dmu`,
`Psi_i=int(L_i)_+ dmu`, `W_i=c_i+r_i S_i`.

The same section measure is used in the derivatives with respect to
individual normals AND to the common rotation. To justify this at
cap/facet coincidences, apply the smooth composition rule for the
locally Lipschitz cap-mass function in its physical cap coefficients.
Each selected generalized gradient pulls back from one consistent
physical cap-gradient set. Convexifying a selection preserves the
same common section mass and first moments; different parameter
components are not assigned independent trace densities.

A finite probability measure `nu_z` on actual primal-dual saddle
pairs `(x,lambda) in V x Delta_N` supplies

`p_zi=int lambda_i dnu_z`, `q_zi=int lambda_i x dnu_z`.

The finite LP-basis gradient proof applies to (2) on its local cube.
At every multiplied contact,

`sum_i lambda_i u_i=0`,
`L_i(z,x)<=0`, `lambda_i L_i(z,x)=0`.                        (4)

Here the representative has `R=I`, so `u_i=v_i` and `x in V`.
As before, these continuous contact points can lie outside `K_z`.

The free offset and integer-tilt equations give

`W_i=sum_z eta_z p_zi`,                                     (5)
`Z_i+r_i Z_i^s=sum_z eta_z z p_zi`.                          (6)

Individual normal variations on the sphere in `V` give, after the
same per-cap Euler cancellation,

`P_V(X_i+r_i X_i^s)-sum_z eta_z q_zi=Psi_i u_i`.             (7)

To verify the cancellation explicitly, before simplifying (7) its
sphere multiplier is `sigma_i u_i`. Take its inner product with
`u_i`, use (5)--(6), and use `L_i=0` on section points and positively
assigned contacts. The result is `sigma_i=-Psi_i`, since `|u_i|=1`.
Projection causes no loss in this calculation because `u_i in V`.

## 5. Exact source-only force and tensor equations

Equations (4)--(6) imply

`sum_i W_i u_i=0`,                                         (8)
`sum_i u_i(Z_i+r_i Z_i^s)^T=0`,                             (9)
`sum_i W_i=sum_z eta_z`.                                   (10)

Define the source matrix

`T=sum_i (X_i+r_i X_i^s)u_i^T`,
`Q=sum_i Psi_i u_i u_i^T`.

Summing (7) after taking its outer product with `u_i` yields
`P_V T=Q`, because the contact term is
`sum_z eta_z int x(sum_i lambda_i u_i)^T dnu_z=0`.
Also `T=T P_V`, since every `u_i` lies in `V`.

Common rotation stationarity supplies the remaining component. For
any skew-symmetric matrix `A`, its infinitesimal velocity is
`dot u_i=A u_i`. The coverage functions (2) have derivative zero
under this variation. Hence normal stationarity gives

`sum_i (X_i+r_i X_i^s) dot A u_i=0`

for every skew-symmetric `A`. This says exactly that `T` is symmetric.
Together with `T=T P_V` and `P_V T=Q`, symmetry implies

`sum_i (X_i+r_i X_i^s)u_i^T
            =sum_i Psi_i u_i u_i^T`.                        (11)

The matrix is positive semidefinite and its trace is the attained
hinge value. In particular,

`v(tau)=sum_i u_i dot (X_i+r_i X_i^s)`.                     (12)

This identity involves only actual source cap and section moments.
It uses no extra frame caps and does not hide supporting-fiber
forces. Its geometric price remains the outside-fiber contact
locations in the variational construction.

Since `tau>0`, `W_i>0` exactly when `c_i>0`: a positive budget
multiplier requires `c_i=tau M>0`, and zero cap mass implies zero
hinge. Thus (8) also proves that zero lies in the relative interior
of the convex hull of the positive-source-mass cap normals. It does
not prove that those caps alone cover whole continuous space.

## 6. A precise covariance consequence, with its limitations

Define a finite measure on labeled source points by

`d nu(i,z,x)=d(mu|H_i)(z,x)+r_i d tau_i(z,x)`.

It has total mass `W=sum_i W_i`. Let the label normal be `U=u_i`
and write `q=(1,z)` for the affine base features. Equations (8)--(11)
say

`int q U^T dnu=0`,
`int x U^T dnu=Q`,
`int U U^T dnu=A:=sum_i W_i u_i u_i^T`.                     (13)

All these moments are finite, including the section terms. Let

`G=int q q^T dnu`, `B=int x q^T dnu`,
`E=int x x^T dnu`, `R_x=E-B G^+ B^T`,

where `G^+` denotes the Moore-Penrose inverse. The matrix `R_x` is
the least-squares residual second moment after fitting a continuous
affine function of the base. This description follows by minimizing
`int|x-Dq|^2 dnu`; null directions of `G` also annihilate `B`, so
the displayed inverse formula is valid even for a lower-dimensional
base support. The residual has the same cross moment `Q` with `U`
by the first equation of (13). Therefore its joint second-moment
matrix with `U` is positive semidefinite, and

`R_x >= Q A^+ Q`.                                          (14)

For an elementary verification, apply
`int|v dot residual-w dot U|^2 dnu>=0`, then minimize over `w`.
If `w` lies in the nullspace of `A`, then `w dot U=0` almost
everywhere and hence `Qw=0`; thus the pseudoinverse formula is
legitimate. A simpler scalar consequence is

`v(tau)^2 <= W trace(R_x)`,                                 (15)

by Cauchy-Schwarz, since `int|U|^2 dnu=W` and `trace Q=v(tau)`.

This is an exact regression inequality with constant one. It does
not control `R_x` in terms of cap masses, and it does not imply
log-concavity of the cap-plus-section weights on integer fibers.
In particular, section variance cannot be silently removed from a
subsequent Brascamp-Lieb or John-ellipsoid argument.

There is a second exact bridge to raw balanced moment bodies. At each
base `z`, choose any feasible mass `t_z`, and let `Q_z` be the compact
body of raw continuous moments of sources `0<=f<=1` having mass
`t_z` and base moment `t_z z`. For every cap, positive-part domination
gives

`Psi_i>=h_Qz(u_i)+t_z(a_i dot z-b_i)`.

At an active whole-space saddle pair, (4) makes the weighted sum of
the last affine terms zero. Consequently

`sum_i W_i Psi_i
 >=sum_z eta_z int [sum_i lambda_i h_Qz(u_i)] dnu_z`.        (15a)

This uses exactly the same source caps and the same circuit weights;
it does not optimize integer tilts separately under an integral. If
`c_z+A_z B_d` is any ellipsoid in `Q_z`, its center cancels under
`sum_i lambda_i u_i=0`, and (15a) yields

`sum_i W_i Psi_i
 >=sum_z eta_z int [sum_i lambda_i |A_z u_i|] dnu_z`.         (15b)

Choosing John ellipsoids is permitted, but no quantitative lower
bound for the weighted right-hand side in terms of `M` is asserted.
This exact bridge has no supporting-fiber defect because its circuits
cover whole continuous space.

## 7. Positive-hinge cap count and exclusion of rank one

Assume additionally that `P=conv(P) intersect Z^n`. This holds for
the positive-volume integer fibers of an actual convex body: by
convexity and Brunn-Minkowski, any integer convex combination of
positive fibers is again a positive fiber. No assumption of full
dimensionality of `conv(P)` is needed.

For whole-space covers whose normals lie in an `r`-dimensional
continuous subspace, some subfamily of at most

`h=2^n(r+1)`

caps still covers `P x R^r`. Here is a proof which keeps the open
complements rigorous. If no such subfamily covered, then each of
the finitely many index subsets `J` of size at most `h` would have
a witness `(z_J,x_J)` with `z_J in P` and `L_i(z_J,x_J)<0` for
every `i in J`. Choose one common continuous cube containing all
these witnesses, and a single `epsilon>0` smaller than all their
finitely many positive margins. Each subfamily of at most `h` of
the CLOSED halfspaces `{L_i<=-epsilon}` would then intersect
`P` times this cube. Apply the finite relative Helly lemma of
candidate 8e3336ffa84bc52d (candidate 8e3336ffa84bc52d)
to `conv(P)` times the cube. Its integer set is exactly `P` times
the cube, and its fiber dimension is `r`. The full family would
intersect there, contradicting whole-space coverage. This proves
the subcover statement using only the proved closed-family lemma.

At a hinge minimizer, EVERY positive-hinge cap belongs to any such
selected subcover. Otherwise replace a positive-hinge cap outside
it by an empty source cap. Coverage and budgets persist, while
the objective strictly decreases, a contradiction. Thus

`number of positive-source-mass caps <=2^n(r+1)`.            (16)

The equivalence between positive mass and positive hinge was proved
in Section 2. Zero-mass caps may occur in the chosen subcover and
are retained; they are not silently removed from whole-space
coverage. They contribute no source measure to its union bound.
Consequently every such minimizing cover satisfies

`M<=sum_(positive caps) c_i<=2^n(r+1) tau M`.                (17)

In particular, a hypothetical whole-space cover with budget strictly
below `gamma_d/2^n` cannot have a rank-one attained minimizing
representative. For if `r=1`, (17) gives `1<=2^(n+1)tau`, whereas
the strict budget gives `2^(n+1)tau<2 gamma_d<=1` for every `d>=1`.
The last inequality follows from `(1+1/d)^d>=2`.

This is a rank exclusion inside the variational system. For `r>=2`,
(17) alone is the familiar weaker Helly count and does not reach
the required constant.

## 8. Scope of the new mechanism

The rank reduction takes place only in the cap-normal parameter
space. The original source, lattice, cap masses, and closed-halfspace
convention are unchanged. Every resulting cap remains an ambient
halfspace, with arbitrary real integer tilt. There is no restriction
to coordinate or vertical cuts.

The proof obtains a selected attained minimizer with normal stress
at every regular budget and with exactly the original cap count.
It does not force its whole-space contacts into `S`, and it supplies
no inequality excluding a budget below `2^(-n) gamma_d`. The new
concrete invariants are (3), the zero source force and base-force
equations (8)--(9), the full positive-semidefinite source tensor
(11), and the regression bound (14).
